# IA Drift Triage

Three findings from the scan, ranked by merge impact:

## 1. `crime_00017` — Route Metadata Drift → **Warn (not block)**

**File:** `src/routes/settings/billing.tsx` (route `/settings/billing`)

The same destination is labelled five different ways:
- Route path: `/settings/billing`
- Component: `PricingPage`
- `metadata.title`: `Plans`
- `<title>`: `Subscription`
- Nav labels: `Plans` (registry.ts) and `Billing` (sidebar.ts)

**Why warn, not block:** The route works — users land on a page. The damage is cognitive: an agent told to "rename the Billing page" will update one label and silently leave four others stale. Confidence is 0.65 (heuristic correlation), so a hard block would punish false positives. Reviewer should pick a canonical name and align the others before merge, but the build isn't broken.

## 2. `crime_00015` — Duplicated Navigation Source → **Warn (not block)**

**Files:** `src/nav/registry.ts` (label "Plans") + `src/nav/sidebar.ts` (label "Billing")

Same `/settings/billing` destination, two nav files, two labels. This is the upstream cause of part of the route_metadata_drift above — the two findings should be fixed together.

**Why warn:** Both navs render fine; the symptom is users seeing inconsistent labels depending on which UI surface they're in. A reviewer should ask "which nav file is the source of truth?" before approving, but it isn't a regression in code paths. If your team has a documented single-source-of-truth nav policy, escalate to block on a per-repo basis.

## 3. `crime_00013` — Docs-Code Drift → **Ignore on this PR (file separately)**

**File:** `docs/teams.md` line 5 links to `./setup.md` (doesn't exist)

**Why ignore for merge gating:** Confidence 0.9, severity `low`, agent_risk 0.51. The link rots a doc, not the product. Blocking a code PR on a stale docs link punishes the wrong author. File a docs-cleanup issue and move on. The exception: if *this* PR touched `docs/teams.md` and introduced the broken link, fix it before merging — but the finding alone doesn't tell you whether the PR is the culprit (no `recency` signal, churn 0).

---

## Suggested merge gate

```
block:    none of the three
warn:    crime_00015, crime_00017  (fix together — same destination)
ignore:  crime_00013  (track as docs hygiene, not a merge gate)
```

The route_metadata_drift + duplicated_navigation_source pair is the one to address pre-merge: they're the same underlying problem (no single source of truth for the `/settings/billing` destination), and an agent editing this area will keep recreating the divergence until it's consolidated.
